teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Begin by asking students if they think economics is related to other subjects they study.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Share their ideas on how economics might be connected to other subjects.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: The concept and scope of economics is well described

teaching_structure.teaching_activities:
Explain the relationship between economics and other subjects, such as:
Mathematics (statistics, calculus)
History (economic history, development)
Geography (resource distribution, trade)
Political Science (economic systems, policy)
Sociology (consumer behavior, social inequality)
Business Studies (management, marketing)
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Take notes on the interdisciplinary nature of economics and its connections to other subjects.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: The concept and scope of economics is well described

teaching_structure.teaching_activities: Divide students into groups and assign each group a subject related to economics. Ask them to prepare a short presentation on how that subject is linked to economics.
teaching_structure.learning_activities: Work in groups to research and present the relationship between economics and their assigned subject.
teaching_structure.assessment_criteria: The concept and scope of economics is well described

Microeconomics: the study of individual economic units (households, firms, markets)
Macroeconomics: the study of the economy as a whole (inflation, unemployment, economic growth)

What to produce? (Which goods and services should be produced?)
How to produce? (What production methods should be used?)
